subject.title: [RFC] Agent Teleconference — minimum-viable scoped meeting primitive with working prototype

question: Should OpenClaw sponsor a first-party agent teleconference lifecycle in core, and if so what storage, transcript privacy, authorization, and handoff contract should it use?
rationale: The requested behavior is plausible and already has prototype evidence, but it creates new core CLI, config, storage, session-state, and security surfaces that repository policy leaves to maintainer product/security intent.

options.title: Sponsor a narrow core design
options.body: Approve a Phase 1 core lifecycle design that uses current session primitives but defines a SQLite-backed storage owner, explicit auth rules, transcript retention/redaction, and focused tests before implementation.

options.title: Defer until handoff contract lands
options.body: Keep this RFC open but block implementation until a lower-level handoff acknowledgment contract replaces the closed unmerged handoff PR.

options.title: Move to plugin or ClawHub first
options.body: Ask for a plugin or ClawHub prototype unless maintainers identify a missing core/plugin API that prevents a safe external implementation.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a narrow core design
recommendation.body: Approve a Phase 1 core lifecycle design that uses current session primitives but defines a SQLite-backed storage owner, explicit auth rules, transcript retention/redaction, and focused tests before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: Steipete provided the existing scoping review and has recent adjacent agent-runtime history, making this the best available routing candidate for the product-direction call.
